name: Paruah
title: Father of Jehoshaphat, Solomon's official
summary: Paruah is a biblical figure primarily known as the father of Jehoshaphat, who was one of King Solomon's twelve district governors. He is mentioned only in connection with his son's office during Solomon's rule over Israel. His name possibly means 'blooming' or 'sprouting'.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as father of Jehoshaphat, Solomon's governor
keyEvents.description: Paruah is mentioned as the father of Jehoshaphat, who was appointed as one of Solomon's twelve district governors responsible for the region of Issachar.

keyEvents.title: Solomon's administrative division
keyEvents.description: King Solomon divided Israel into twelve districts with governors who were to provide supplies for the king's household. Paruah's son Jehoshaphat served in one of these districts.

keyEvents.title: Solomon's wealth and wisdom
keyEvents.description: During Solomon's reign, when Paruah's son Jehoshaphat served as governor, Israel experienced a time of great prosperity and peace.

keyEvents.title: Supplies for the king's table
keyEvents.description: Each of the twelve governors, including Jehoshaphat son of Paruah, was responsible for supplying the king's household with food and necessities for one month each year.
